Inclination

in-kluh-NAY-shun -- shares a root with 'recline,' meaning to lean back. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Inclination is a natural tendency or preference to act or feel in a particular way.

She had a natural inclination toward solving puzzles rather than reading fiction.

Worked Example

Given a free afternoon, one student always heads straight for the chess club, while her twin always heads for the art studio, without either of them ever having to think twice about it.

That built-in pull toward one activity over another is exactly what inclination means. Unlike 'obligation,' which is a duty imposed from outside, inclination comes from a person's own natural preference.

How Inclination Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

tendency

tendency: a habitual way of behaving

penchant

penchant: a strong or habitual liking for something

predisposition

predisposition: a tendency to behave in a particular way

Antonyms

aversion

aversion: a strong dislike or unwillingness toward something

reluctance

reluctance: unwillingness to do something

How Strong Is It? — tendency → inclination → penchant

tendency vs. inclination

tendency vs. inclination: Tendency is a more everyday, neutral word than inclination -- tendency can describe any habitual pattern, while inclination specifically implies a personal, often deep-seated preference.

penchant vs. inclination

penchant vs. inclination: Penchant can feel stronger than inclination: inclination is a general leaning toward something, while penchant implies a fondness so strong it borders on a passion.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — in-

prefix — in-: toward (Latin)

root — -clin-

root — -clin-: to bend, lean (Latin (clinare))

suffix — -ation

suffix — -ation: the act or result of; forms a noun (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin clinare meant 'to bend or lean,' and the suffix -ation turns the action into a noun. An inclination is literally 'a leaning toward' something -- the same root that gives us recline.

Use the root in a new word: recline

Use the root in a new word: recline: After the long hike, she was relieved to finally recline in a comfortable chair.

Word Choice

Inclination describes a personal leaning or preference, often paired with 'toward' or 'to,' as in 'an inclination toward caution' or 'no inclination to argue.'
